ai.literal: Evening? not-you; united-ones' life consuming time you, bless-you, time!
ai.translation: You are not merely the evening; you are the deadly hour that consumes the lives of those parted from their lovers. Oh time, may you live long!
ai.modern: நீ வெறும் மாலைப்பொழுது இல்லை; காதலரை விட்டுப் பிரிந்தவர்களின் உயிரை உண்ணும் நேரம் நீ. பொழுதே, நீ வாழ்வாயாக!
ai.explanation: The speaker addresses the evening directly, expressing the intense pain of separation. She says it is no longer just a normal evening, but a deadly time that consumes the lives of those parted from their lovers. The word 'வாழி' (may you live) is used ironically or in distress, highlighting her helplessness against the overwhelming sorrow brought by the time of day.

ai.literal: Sad-eyed-you-are, hail, bewildered evening! Our lover like, hard-hearted-is-it your companion?
ai.translation: Hail, bewildered evening! You have sad, dim eyes. Is your companion as hard-hearted as my lover?
ai.modern: மயக்கத்தைத் தரும் மாலையே! நீயும் துன்பம் நிறைந்த கண்களை உடையவளாக இருக்கிறாய். என் காதலரைப் போலவே உன்னுடைய துணையும் இரக்கமற்றதோ?
ai.explanation: The heroine addresses the evening, projecting her own sorrow onto the time of day. She calls the evening 'bewildered' (மருள்) and notes its 'sad eyes' (புன்கண்ணை), referring to the dimming, gloomy light of dusk. Seeing the evening's sorrowful state, she wonders if its companion has abandoned it and is as hard-hearted (வன்கண்ணது) as her own lover. This personification beautifully captures her intense loneliness and longing.

ai.literal: Dew budding, sorrow taking evening, anguish budding, pain to grow comes.
ai.translation: The evening, bringing dew and sorrow, arrives causing anguish to bud and pain to grow.
ai.modern: பனி துளிர்த்துத் துன்பத்தைக் கொண்டுள்ள மாலைப்பொழுதானது, என் துயரம் துளிர்த்துத் துன்பம் மேலும் வளரும்படியாக வருகின்றது.
ai.explanation: The speaker laments the arrival of evening, a time that worsens the pain of separation. The word 'pani' can mean dew, chill, or tears; here 'dew' fits best as it naturally buds in the evening. Similarly, 'tuni' can mean disgust or sulking, but in this context of separation, it means deep anguish. She describes the evening as bringing dew and carrying sorrow. As this evening arrives, it causes her own deep anguish to bud and her pain to grow even larger, linking the natural formation of evening dew with the sprouting of her inner grief.

ai.literal: Lover when absent, evening, at the execution ground enemies like, comes.
ai.translation: When my lover is absent, the evening approaches like ruthless enemies at the execution ground.
ai.modern: காதலர் அருகில் இல்லாத போது, இந்த மாலைப் பொழுது கொலைக்களத்தில் நிற்கும் பகைவர்களைப் போல என்னை வதைக்க வருகிறது.
ai.explanation: The speaker expresses the unbearable agony of twilight when separated from her lover. The evening, which normally brings lovers together, is personified as a deadly threat. The word 'ஏதிலர்' generally means strangers, but placed in a 'கொலைக்களம்' (execution ground), it takes the specific sense of merciless executioners or enemies. This stark image conveys how the loneliness of the evening feels like an impending, inescapable death.

ai.literal: To the morning done good what indeed? What indeed I to the evening done enmity?
ai.translation: What good have I done to the morning? And what harm have I done to the evening?
ai.modern: நான் காலைப் பொழுதிற்குச் செய்த நன்மை என்ன? மாலைப் பொழுதிற்குச் செய்த தீமைதான் என்ன?
ai.explanation: The speaker contrasts her experience of morning and evening during her lover's absence. Morning brings her relief and hope, making her wonder what good deed she did to earn its favor. Evening, however, intensifies her loneliness and sorrow, prompting her to ask what harm she ever did to make it torment her so. The words 'நன்று' (good) and 'பகை' (enmity or harm) highlight the stark difference in how the two times of day affect her lovesick heart.

ai.literal: Evening pain causing, lover unseparated time, known I am not.
ai.translation: I did not know that evening causes such pain, back when my lover had not parted from me.
ai.modern: என் காதலர் என்னை விட்டுப் பிரியாமல் இருந்த காலத்தில், மாலைப் பொழுது இவ்வளவு துன்பம் செய்யும் என்பதை நான் அறிந்திருக்கவில்லை.
ai.explanation: The speaker laments the intense sorrow brought by the evening now that she is separated from her lover. She states that when they were together, she was completely unaware of the evening's capacity to cause such pain. The word 'காலை' here means 'time' or 'period' rather than 'morning', referring to the time before his departure.

ai.literal: Morning having budded, day all mature bud having become, evening blooms this disease.
ai.translation: This disease of love buds in the morning, swells into a mature bud all through the day, and blossoms fully in the evening.
ai.modern: இந்தக் காதல் நோயானது காலையில் அரும்பாகி, பகல் முழுவதும் முதிர்ந்த மொட்டாகி, மாலையில் முழுமையாக மலர்கிறது.
ai.explanation: The poet uses a beautiful botanical metaphor to describe the progression of lovesickness throughout the day. The pain of separation is compared to a flower that begins as a tiny bud in the morning ('arumpi'). As the day passes, it swells into a mature bud ('pōtu'), and when evening arrives, it fully blossoms ('malarum') into intense suffering. This illustrates how the loneliness of evening makes the pangs of love feel most acute.

ai.literal: Fire like to evening messenger having become cowherd's flute like killing weapon.
ai.translation: Acting as a messenger for the fire-like evening, the cowherd's flute is like a deadly weapon.
ai.modern: நெருப்பைப் போலச் சுடும் மாலைப் பொழுதிற்குத் தூதனாக வந்து, இந்த ஆயனின் புல்லாங்குழல் என்னைக் கொல்லும் ஆயுதமாகி விட்டது.
ai.explanation: The speaker, suffering in the absence of her lover, feels the approaching evening like a burning fire. The sound of the cowherd's flute announces the arrival of this painful time. To her, the sweet music of the flute no longer brings joy, but resembles a deadly weapon that has come as a messenger of the fiery evening to take her life. The word 'போலும்' (like) is used twice, comparing the evening to fire and the flute to a weapon.

ai.translation: When evening comes spreading and confuses the mind, this whole town becomes bewildered and suffers sorrow.
ai.modern: அறிவு மயங்கும்படி மாலைக்காலம் பரவி வரும்போது, இந்த ஊரும் மயக்கமடைந்து துன்பத்தை அனுபவிக்கும்.
ai.explanation: The heroine observes the overwhelming effect of the evening on her surroundings. The word 'மதி' (mind) refers to how the arrival of dusk disorients the intellect and stirs up deep emotional distress. Projecting her own inner turmoil onto the world around her, she feels that as the evening spreads ('மாலை படர்தரும் போழ்து'), the entire town ('பதி') shares in her bewilderment and suffers the same sorrow ('பைதல் உழக்கும்').

ai.literal: Wealth-nature possessor (ACC) having thought, confusing evening will perish my unperishing life.
ai.translation: Thinking of him whose nature is to seek wealth, my stubborn life will finally perish in this bewildering evening.
ai.modern: பொருள் தேடும் இயல்பை உடைய என் தலைவரை நினைத்து, இதுவரை இறக்காத என் உயிர் இந்த மயக்கத்தைத் தரும் மாலைப் பொழுதில் இறந்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: The speaker laments the unbearable pain of evening during her lover's absence. She describes him as someone whose nature is tied to wealth, as he left her to seek it. Her life, which has stubbornly refused to end despite her prolonged suffering, will finally be extinguished by the bewildering sorrow brought by the evening.
